title: Fractionalized Fermi Liquid and d-wave Superconductivity in Ba2CuO3+x
authors: M. S. Laad, S. Koley, A. Taraphder
abstract: Strongly enhanced superconductivity (SC) (Tc = 73 K) in Ba2CuO3+x (BCO) challenges the longheld paradigm of the irrelevance of the dz2-like states in cuprates. Using tight-binding band structure plus dynamical mean-field theory (TB+DMFT), we find that a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FFL) is the normal state for the parameters realistic for BCO. Transport properties exhibit strange metal behavior above Tcoh~38 K, supporting a direct instability of this strange metal to SC. Irrelevance of one-fermion inter-band mixing, itself a non-trivial consequence of the FFL state, preferentially enhances two-fermion hopping processes and provides a novel route for both SC and competing excitonic order(s) arising directly from the FFL. The proposed scenario also clarifies the role of dz2 band in shaping the physical responses of BCO.
summary: This theoretical work models high-$T_c$ superconductivity in BCO using an Orbital Selective Mott Phase framework. It argues that the normal state is a Fractionalized Fermi Liquid, which drives $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave superconductivity through coherent, two-fermion pair hopping between correlated orbitals. The findings provide a mechanism that explains the strange metal transport properties observed above $T_c$.
main_problem: The paper addresses the mechanism behind the high-temperature superconductivity in $	ext{Ba}_2	ext{CuO}_{3+x}$ (BCO), challenging the assumption that $	ext{d}_{z^2}$-like states are irrelevant in cuprates.
main_result: The normal state is proposed to be a Fractionalized Fermi Liquid (FFL) driven by an Orbital Selective Mott Phase (OSMP), leading to $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave superconductivity via coherent two-fermion pair hopping between orbitals.
method: The study employs a combination of Tight-binding band structure plus Dynamical Mean Field Theory ($	ext{TB}+	ext{DMFT}$) to model correlation effects, followed by strong-coupling Eliashberg theory analysis for superconductivity.
model_or_system: The system is BCO, modeled by a two-orbital Hubbard model exhibiting an OSMP, where $	ext{d}_{z^2}$ ($	ext{b}$-band) states are Mott localized while $	ext{d}_{x^2-y^2}$ ($	ext{a}$-band) states remain metallic.
key_observables: Strange metal resistivity ($ho_{dc} \propto T$), non-Drude optical conductivity ($\sigma_{xx} \propto \omega^{-\alpha}$), and the superconducting gap structure.
important_parameters: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c = 73$ K), characteristic temperature $T \approx 38$ K, and the BCS gap-to-$T_c$ ratio ($y \approx 4.3 - 4.5$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the OSMP framework, which dynamically blocks coherent $a-b$ mixing, making inter-chain two-fermion hopping processes relevant for pairing.
figures_summary: Figure 4 shows the total low-energy intra-band optical conductivity $\sigma_{xx}(q=0, \omega; T)$ versus Temperature, illustrating the temperature dependence in the strange metal regime.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the FFL normal state using $	ext{TB}+	ext{DMFT}$ diagnostics (strange metal behavior). It then analyzes the superconducting instability by deriving an effective residual interaction Hamiltonian ($H_{	ext{res}}$) that mediates $d$-wave pair hopping between the two bands, predicting $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave SC.
why_interesting: The concept of FFL and OSMP provides a highly correlated, non-Fermi liquid description of the normal state, which is a key area of modern condensed matter theory relevant to understanding exotic quantum phases.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

In panel (b), spectral weight van- ishes at EF(= 0) (see text), resulting in an incoherent (lower) Hubbard band.

FIG. 3: (Color Online) dc resistivity ρdc(T ) (in arbitrary units) for Ba2CuO3+x (Tc = 73 K) shows a smooth crossover from T -linear behavior above 60 K to an apparent normal ρdc(T ) ∝T 2) form below 30 K. Extrapolation of the T -linear part cuts the T -axis at T ≈38 K, marking a pseudogapped metal coexisting with localized b-fermion moments.

FIG. 5: (Color Online) Non-interacting tight-binding electronic structure of the eﬀective two-band model: (a) bare energy dispersion along high-symmetry paths in the two-dimensional Brillouin zone (Γ–M–X–Γ), with the Fermi level set to zero (EF = 0 eV, horizontal dotted line); (b) corresponding bare orbital-resolved density of states (DOS), showing prominent Van Hove singularities near the band edges and close to EF (vertical dotted line). (c),(d) show the Fermi pockets in BCO: the b = dz2-like band shows clear one-dimensional character, while the a = dx2−y2-band gives four hole pockets, centered about (±π, ±π) in the ﬁrst Brillouin zone.
